title: Control fractional regularity with mass-weighted heat entropy
statement: For0<s<1 define E_s=s(1-s)sum int_0^infinity[H(f_i)-H(P_tau^i f_i)]tau^-1-s d tau=(1-s)int tau^-s I_m(P_tau f)d tau. N=n1+n2,K=3N/2,I0=I_m give0<=E_s<=K^(1-s)I0^s/s by I_m(P_tau f)<=min(I0,K/tau). The lower bound E_s>=2^s Gamma(2-s)sum m_i^-s ||sqrt(f_i)||dotHs^2 uses Fourier convention -Delta multiplier|xi|^2, hence f_i in L^(3/(3-2s)). Heat entropy tensorizes on probability products, is superadditive over marginals by heat mutual information, and has additive product first variation at its stated normalization. These are initial/functional inequalities, not a collision-time Lyapunov or global bound. Actual n_i are not silently set to one.
